subject: Operational handshake: hosted API latency SLOs and evidence timeline
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Wu <alice.wu@finnect.com>, ops@finnect.com
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 28 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Operational handshake: hosted API latency SLOs and evidence timeline

Hi Alice —

Thanks again for taking the call yesterday. As discussed, Finnect is asking us to codify the hosted API latency commitments (p50 / p95) and the operational evidence we'll supply during the onboarding canary and first 30 days. I wanted to outline a concrete handshake so procurement and your ops team have what they need.

Quick summary of what Redwood proposes:
- SLO targets (hosted API, us-west region): p50 <= 60ms, p95 <= 220ms measured over a rolling 1-hour window with 5-minute sampling cadence.
- Canary period: 10 business days of production traffic (canary routing to a pinned pool) followed by 20 business days of standard routing before final go/no-go.
- Evidence package: aggregated p50/p95 time-series, request-level tail traces for sampled requests, KV cache hit-rate, and request distribution by sequence length.

I've attached an "slo-evidence-checklist.pdf" and a short canary plan. Can you confirm: (1) the proposed measurement window is acceptable to Finnect; (2) whether you need us to provide raw logs vs. summarized CSVs; and (3) procurement requirements for signoff (DocuSign link or PO)?

If helpful, Kimberly and Aditya are copied to align on telemetry and whether we should run a short synthetic before canary start.

Thanks,
Priya
Priya Natarajan
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0182

[attachment: sLO-evidence-checklist.pdf (pdf)]
From: Alice Wu <alice.wu@finnect.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@finnect.com>, ops@finnect.com
Date: Sun, 28 Sep 2025 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Operational handshake: hosted API latency SLOs and evidence timeline

Priya —

Appreciate the clear summary. A few clarifying items from ops/procurement: 
1) Measurement window: procurement expects contract language to reference daily aggregated p50/p95 computed over a rolling 1-hour measurement window (we need the legal wording). The 5-minute sampling cadence is fine but we will still expect daily exports for the contract.
2) Evidence: ops prefers summarized CSVs and a weekly raw logs export for the canary (s3 link). Raw traces only on request for specific incidents.
3) Canary: 10 business days sounds reasonable. Will Finnect be able to request a 48-hour extension if we detect a config-related noise event?

Also, does Redwood provide a pre-canary synthetic run to confirm baseline? If so, please include timing in the plan — procurement wants a final signoff milestone before the DocuSign signature.

Thanks — will loop in procurement for the DocuSign flow.

Best,
Alice
Alice Wu
Head of Site Reliability, Finnect Inc.
alice.wu@finnect.com
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 28 Sep 2025 12:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Operational handshake: hosted API latency SLOs and evidence timeline

Priya / Aditya —

Per Alice's ask: we can produce both the daily aggregated p50/p95 (derived from 5-min buckets) and a weekly S3 export of sampled raw logs for the canary. Notes from infra side: 
- Measurement details: our hosted telemetry calculates p50/p95 using continuous 5-minute windows and then computes rolling 1-hour aggregates (so there is no discrepancy between raw and aggregated numbers). We'll include a short appendix in the evidence package that states binning and sampling rules (attached spreadsheet: measurement-definitions.xlsx).
- Synthetic run: we recommend a 24-hour pre-canary synthetic with a traffic shape that mirrors your production percentiles (20% long-sequence work, 80% short). This helps calibrate KV cache warmup and batching behavior.
- 48-hour extension: operations can gate the canary with a single 48-hour extension if noise is identified; we will record the extension as part of the evidence timeline.

Aditya — can you please prepare the canary routing snippet and the plan page (10 business days + extension clause) so I can attach it to the DocuSign package?

Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Director, Customer Reliability
kimberly.park@redwood.ai
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Wu <alice.wu@finnect.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 28 Sep 2025 14:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Operational handshake: hosted API latency SLOs and evidence timeline

Alice / Team —

Attached is the canary plan PDF (canary-plan-202510.pdf) and a short routing snippet. Key operational callouts: 
- Canary start proposed: 2025-10-06 (Tuesday) with 24-hour synthetic starting 2025-10-03.
- Canary routing: 10% of Finnect production traffic pinned to a reserved pool for the first 48 hours, then scaled to 30% for remaining business days. After the 10 business day period, we shift to full traffic unless there is a recorded extension or canary failures.
- Evidence deliverables: daily p50/p95 CSVs uploaded to the Finnect S3 bucket (s3://finnect-onboarding/slo-exports/), weekly raw log tarball, and a closing document with traces for any p95 regressions.

Next steps for procurement: Priya — please confirm whether we should generate a DocuSign package with the canary plan + evidence checklist or wait for a PO before DocuSign. Once we have procurement's preference I'll prepare the final package and push the DocuSign link (I've stubbed a placeholder link in the metadata).

Thanks,
Aditya
Aditya Rao
Technical Program Manager, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai
